partnershipPlan: Two patient partners and a family caregiver review the call script and the information posters before the first step; oncologists from two clinics and the palliative care nurse join the oversight group that reviews waiting times monthly.
socialListening: No social media listening; the centre's patient feedback forms from the last year are read for comments about palliative care referral.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I thought palliative care was for the last days; nobody told me it could help while I was still on chemotherapy.
items.implication: The nurse's call explains that palliative care runs alongside treatment.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: I do not want a computer telling my patient they are dying before I have had that conversation myself.
items.implication: Keep the opt-out window and let oncologists add a note to the referral.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: We met the palliative team a week before he died; they were wonderful, and we wished we had met them months earlier.
items.implication: Report end-of-life care among patients who die, not only visit timing.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: If thirty extra referrals arrive in one week, the people who need us most will wait longest.
items.implication: Monitor waiting time monthly as a balancing measure and allow the rollout to slow.

items.quote: Composite paraphrase: Earlier referral only helps if the community team hears about the patient before the crisis.
items.implication: Share the referral with the community hospice when the patient agrees.

summary: Five composite voices on meaning, ownership of the conversation, timing, capacity and community follow-through.
